For example, imagine a warm air mass over a lake in springtime. The warm air is lighter and rises. It moves up into the atmosphere, creating an area of lower pressure near the surface. Cold air from surrounding areas is denser, so it moves in to fill the space left behind by the rising warm air. This cold air moves in a direction that is generally opposite to the path of the warm air, creating a cold front.
